sources.entry: Manifest - Complete backend that fits into 1 YAML file. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Nodejs

summary.one_liner: Manifest LLM Gateway is an open-source, MIT-licensed gateway that exposes many LLM providers (API keys, subscriptions, local models) through a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint with routing, logging, and fallback.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes an LLM gateway for AI agents and apps that connects API keys, subscription logins, local models, and custom OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible endpoints to one OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Requests can be sent with "model": "auto" so Manifest picks the model, or routed to a specific provider. It claims full request and error body logging, cost tracking with notifications and limits, and fallback to other models when a query fails. The README lists 35 built-in provider connections (including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, AWS Bedrock, DeepSeek, Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, OpenRouter, Groq, and others) and 18 subscription flows, and notes that provider catalogs are discovered dynamically. A cloud version is also offered at app.manifest.build. The README is a product overview with a short self-hosting section; the Docker install command in the extracted README is garbled and does not show a usable command.
use_cases: route requests across multiple LLM providers
fallback to another model when a request fails
use local models like Ollama or LM Studio behind one API
connect AI agents to many models without vendor lock-in
how_to_run: Self-hosted: run the Manifest Docker image (the README says it ships as a Docker image; the exact command is not legible in the extracted text)
Or follow one of the linked deployment guides: Railway, Render, DigitalOcean, AWS, GCP, Fly.io, Coolify, Easypanel, Heroku, Koyeb, or Apple Containers
Cloud: go to app.manifest.build and follow the guide
The npm-based self-hosting path is no longer supported
notable: Single OpenAI-compatible endpoint across 300+ models from 35 built-in provider connections
Subscription flows let existing ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, and similar plans be reused as providers
"model": "auto" lets the gateway choose the model per query
Full body logs for success and error responses, plus per-dollar cost tracking
caveats: Volume-backed deployment templates are single-instance; horizontal scaling requires S3-compatible storage
The old npm-based self-hosting path is no longer supported; Docker or the listed deployment guides are required
Some deployment targets need external S3-compatible storage configured during setup
keywords: use many models with one api key
route requests to the cheapest model
switch llm providers without code changes
local and cloud models in one api
